overview: L'Oréal is the world's largest beauty company, with FY2025 sales of EUR44.05 billion generated from a single vocation -- 'beauty, nothing but beauty' -- sold through four global divisions (L'Oréal Luxe, Consumer Products, Dermatological Beauty, Professional Products) and roughly 40 major international brands (L'Oréal Paris, Lancome, Kerastase, CeraVe, La Roche-Posay, Yves Saint Laurent Beaute, Prada Beauty, Garnier, Maybelline, NYX, Aesop, Medik8, among others). The Group operates in over 150 countries through five geographic regions (Europe, North America, North Asia, SAPMENA-SSA, Latin America), manufactures in 37 of its own factories, and is majority-influenced by the founding Bettencourt Meyers family (via the Tethys holding company), which provides decades of governance stability alongside listed-company discipline.

business_model.summary: L'Oréal earns nearly all of its revenue from selling branded cosmetics, skincare, haircare and fragrance products through a multi-channel distribution network (mass retail, selective/department-store, professional salons, dermo-pharmacy, duty-free/Travel Retail, and a rapidly growing e-commerce channel now ~30% of sales). Growth is driven by volume plus price/mix (premiumisation), funded reinvestment into advertising & promotion (~32% of sales) and R&I (~3% of sales), with an active bolt-on M&A programme adding brands/licences in high-growth adjacencies (medicalised skincare, K-beauty, styling, ultra-luxury fragrance/licensed fashion-house beauty). Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional/repeat-purchase consumer-goods revenue rather than contractual/recurring, but very high brand loyalty and daily-use product categories (skincare, haircare) give it staple-like repeat-purchase characteristics within a discretionary/semi-discretionary category.

revenue_streams.name: Consumer Products
revenue_streams.description: Mass-market brands (L'Oreal Paris, Garnier, Maybelline, NYX); FY2025 sales EUR16.09bn, +3.5% LFL, +0.7% reported; the largest division by sales but slowest-growing

revenue_streams.name: L'Oreal Luxe
revenue_streams.description: Prestige brands (Lancome, YSL Beaute, Prada Beauty, Armani, Helena Rubinstein, Aesop, Kiehl's, recently added Kering Beaute brands Creed/Bottega Veneta/Balenciaga and a future Gucci licence); FY2025 sales EUR15.60bn, +2.8% LFL; H1 2026 LFL accelerated to +5.4% as China/Travel Retail stabilised

revenue_streams.name: Dermatological Beauty
revenue_streams.description: Dermo-cosmetics sold via pharmacies and mass/medical channels (La Roche-Posay, CeraVe, SkinCeuticals, Vichy, recently acquired Dr.G); FY2025 sales EUR7.20bn, +5.5% LFL; H1 2026 adjusted LFL +10.6% as CeraVe's turnaround continued and SkinCeuticals passed EUR1bn

revenue_streams.name: Professional Products
revenue_streams.description: Salon-distributed haircare/colour (Kerastase, Redken, Matrix, L'Oreal Professionnel, recently acquired Color Wow); FY2025 sales EUR5.16bn (first time over EUR5bn), +7.5% LFL; H1 2026 adjusted LFL +11.6%, the Group's best-performing division

business_model.customer_type: B2C through retail/e-commerce (mass, selective, dermo-pharmacy, duty-free) and B2B2C through professional hair salons; no single retail customer is individually material enough to be disclosed as a concentration risk, though large omnichannel retailers (Amazon, Sephora/LVMH, Walmart, Douyin/Tmall in China) have increasing negotiating leverage
business_model.geographic_mix: Europe 33.7% of FY2025 sales (+4.4% LFL), North America 26.6% (+3.4% LFL but -0.7% reported on FX), North Asia 22.9% (+0.5% LFL, dragged by China Travel Retail), SAPMENA-SSA 9.3% (+10.9% LFL, fastest-growing region), Latin America 7.4% (+8.3% LFL); emerging markets are ~17% of sales but delivered ~40% of total sales growth in 2025
business_model.unit_economics: FY2025 gross margin 74.3% (up 10bp despite tariff headwinds, offset by price/mix and operating efficiency); operating margin 20.2% (up 20bp), with all four divisions posting operating margins above 21% in 2025 (Dermatological Beauty highest at 26.1% FY/28.4% H1 2026); A&P spend ~32% of sales funds brand equity and is the primary lever management flexes to protect margin; e-commerce (~30% of sales) carries different channel economics (higher marketing intensity, lower physical retail margin erosion) than it did a decade ago when it was under 6%

main_competitors: fast-growing indie/DTC brands (Rare Beauty, Fenty Beauty, e.l.f. Beauty) and Chinese local champions (Proya, Bloomage, Winona)
competitive_position.market_position: Global #1 in beauty by sales (2024 WWD Beauty Top 100: L'Oreal ~USD47bn vs Unilever ~USD27bn, Estee Lauder/P&G beauty ~USD15bn each, ahead of LVMH, Chanel, Beiersdorf, Shiseido, Coty, Puig); L'Oreal became the #1 player in North Asia (including China) for the first time in 2025, achieving market leadership across all five of its geographic regions; the only beauty major with meaningful scale across all four price tiers (mass, dermo-pharmacy, professional salon, luxury) and all distribution channels simultaneously

moat_factors.description: ~40 major international brands spanning every price point, category (hair, skin, makeup, fragrance) and channel provide resilience -- weakness in one division/region (e.g., Luxe/Travel Retail/China in 2023-2025) is offset by strength elsewhere (Professional Products, Dermatological Beauty, SAPMENA-SSA), a structural advantage single-category or single-region peers (Coty, Shiseido) lack

EUR1.38bn (3% of sales) R&I spend, 22 research centres, 725 patents filed in 2025 (record), and decades of dermatologist/pharmacist channel relationships underpin brands like La Roche-Posay, CeraVe and SkinCeuticals that compete on clinically-substantiated efficacy claims difficult for indie/DTC entrants to replicate quickly

moat_factors.factor: Scale in advertising and shelf/channel access
moat_factors.description: ~EUR14.2bn annual A&P spend (32% of sales) funds global media buying power, retailer relationships and Beauty Tech/AI-driven precision marketing (BETIQ, ModiFace, Beauty Genius) that smaller challengers cannot match, reinforcing brand prominence across both offline and online shelf space

37 owned factories sited close to end markets (e.g., Gauchy fragrance plant capacity doubled in 2025) plus 160 distribution centres support service levels and cost efficiency at a scale smaller rivals cannot replicate, though this is a smaller advantage than brand/innovation moats and adds fixed-cost/Seveso-site operational risk

The founding Bettencourt Meyers family (via Tethys, L'Oreal's largest shareholder) has backed the same management philosophy for decades, enabling patient, counter-cyclical bolt-on M&A (a record year for deals in 2025: Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Kering Beaute brands, increased Galderma stake) that short-termist peers under activist pressure may struggle to match

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on discretionary prestige/Travel Retail spending in Asia -- North Asia LFL growth was just +0.5% in FY2025 and L'Oreal Luxe sales were flat (+0.0% reported) as the Chinese/Asian duty-free selective market remained challenged, though recovery began in H2 2025/H1 2026

North America sales fell -0.7% reported in FY2025 (though +3.4% LFL) partly on FX and a mid-2026 IT/ERP system transition in the US (new system went live 8 June 2026) that carries execution risk during the cutover window

Exposure to fast-moving, lower-overhead indie, DTC and influencer-led brands (Rare Beauty, Fenty Beauty, e.l.f. Beauty) and e-commerce-native Chinese domestic champions (Proya, Bloomage) that can launch and iterate faster than a company L'Oreal's size, pressuring share in makeup and some skincare sub-segments
Growing dependence on Amazon and other large online marketplaces for incremental growth increases channel concentration risk and gives powerful retail partners pricing/data leverage

Integration risk from an unusually acquisitive 2025-2026 (Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Kering Beaute/Creed/Bottega Veneta/Balenciaga, incremental Galderma stake, Innovist in India, future Gucci licence from mid-2027) raises execution and goodwill/intangible impairment risk if any newly acquired brand underperforms

growth_drivers: Premiumisation of beauty globally, particularly in haircare (Kerastase, Redken) and the ultra-premium/Couture fragrance segment (Yves Saint Laurent Libre -- the world's #1 women's fragrance -- Prada Paradigme, Valentino Born in Roma)

Dermocosmetics/skincare science positioning (La Roche-Posay, CeraVe, SkinCeuticals, Vichy, and newly acquired Dr.G and Medik8) riding rising consumer demand for clinically substantiated, 'longevity'-oriented skin health products

Continued e-commerce penetration (almost 6x since 2015, crossing the 30% of sales mark for the first time in 2025) and omnichannel/online-offline integration, which outperforms in-store growth across nearly every region and division

Emerging-market expansion: emerging markets were ~17% of FY2025 sales but ~40% of total sales growth, led by SAPMENA-SSA (+10.9% LFL, fastest-growing region) and India (Innovist acquisition pending), Brazil, Vietnam and the GCC

Record 2025 M&A/licensing activity to fill portfolio gaps: Dr.G (Korean dermocosmetics), Medik8 (UK medicalised skincare) and Color Wow (US premium styling) acquired in 2025; Kering Beaute (House of Creed plus 50-year Bottega Veneta/Balenciaga licences) closed 31 March 2026; a 50-year exclusive Gucci beauty licence signed July 2026 (effective 1 July 2027); increased Galderma stake to 20% (closed February 2026); Innovist majority stake agreed June 2026 to expand in India; and a longevity joint venture with Kering

AI and Beauty Tech investment (record 2025/2026 tech spend; expanded NVIDIA partnership for AI-driven computational chemistry/formulation discovery; OpenAI collaboration on agentic commerce) aimed at accelerating R&I, precision marketing and personalised consumer experiences

China and Travel Retail gradual stabilisation -- North Asia LFL growth accelerated from flat in H1 2025 to +4% in H2 2025 and the H1 2026 report cites a 'gradually improving' Chinese selective market with L'Oreal outperforming nearly three-fold

Professional Products' omnichannel salon strategy and premium haircare innovation (Kerastase Gloss Absolu, Redken Shades ALK) sustaining the Group's fastest-growing, highest-margin-trajectory division

business.description: Constant pressure from large global peers, local/regional brands and new digital-economy entrants; failure to anticipate shifts in consumer preference (personalisation, smart devices, sustainability) could erode sales and growth, per the Group's own risk disclosure

business.risk: China / North Asia and Travel Retail sensitivity
business.description: North Asia LFL growth was just +0.5% in FY2025 (L'Oreal Luxe flat) as the Chinese/Asian duty-free selective market and Travel Retail channel remained structurally weak; while H2 2025/H1 2026 showed gradual recovery, any renewed China slowdown, Travel Retail disruption or Middle East conflict spillover (noted as impacting SAPMENA Gulf consumption in H1 2026) would disproportionately hit the highest-margin Luxe division
Adverse product-use events, influencer controversies or misinformation can spread rapidly across digital/social media in 14+ languages and damage brand equity across the 40-brand portfolio

business.risk: Developments in sales channels / e-commerce and retailer concentration
business.description: Rapid shift toward e-commerce (~30% of sales) and growing reliance on large marketplaces (Amazon) and Chinese platforms (Tmall, Douyin) increases exposure to platform algorithm changes, fee structures and retailer bargaining power

business.risk: Human resources and organisational / integration risk
business.description: A record pace of 2025-2026 acquisitions (Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Kering Beaute, Innovist) and IT system transformation (new US ERP went live June 2026) raises near-term integration and change-management risk

financial.description: L'Oreal's single most material financial risk per its own disclosure; a strong euro versus USD and emerging-market currencies has repeatedly turned solid like-for-like growth into flat or negative reported growth (e.g., North America -0.7% reported vs +3.4% LFL in FY2025; H1 2026 currency drag of -2.8% on sales); extrapolating the 30 June 2026 EUR/USD rate of 1.1395 implies roughly a -0.6% full-year 2026 currency headwind on sales

2025 tariffs had a 20bp negative impact on gross margin, offset by price/mix and efficiency; further escalation in US or other trade policy could pressure margins or require supply-chain reconfiguration

financial.risk: Financial equity risk (Sanofi and Galderma stakes)
financial.description: L'Oreal holds a 7.27% stake in Sanofi and a 20% stake in Galderma (increased from 10%, closed February 2026); a sustained decline in either company's share price or dividend (Sanofi dividends fell 22% YoY in 2025 after L'Oreal trimmed its stake in February 2025) would affect L'Oreal's reported finance income and balance sheet

Large non-amortised brand and goodwill balances from an unusually acquisitive 2025-2026 (Kering Beaute, Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow) are tested annually for impairment; underperformance of any acquired brand could trigger write-downs

regulatory.description: Exposure to REACH/CLP cosmetic safety regulation, competition law, anti-corruption rules and economic sanctions across 75+ countries in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical and regulatory environment, raising compliance costs

H1 2026 non-recurring items included EUR169m related to product liability lawsuits; the Group flags elevated US product-liability risk given class-action exposure, high defence costs, jury unpredictability and intense media coverage
Tightening global data regulation (GDPR, CCPA, LGPD, EU NIS2/CRA) and emerging AI governance requirements raise compliance costs as L'Oreal scales its Beauty Tech/AI ambitions
France's 2025/2026 exceptional corporate tax surcharge added EUR253m (2025) and a further EUR188m (H1 2026) in non-recurring tax costs

macro.description: Group's own top-rated business risk: geopolitical tensions, prolonged inflation, trade disputes/tariffs or sovereign debt crises in markets where it generates significant sales (North America 26.6%, North Asia 22.9%, Latin America 7.4% of FY2025 sales) could materially affect business

Beauty has proven relatively resilient as a 'consumer safe haven' through past downturns, but prestige/Luxe and Travel Retail segments are more cyclically exposed to high-end discretionary spending than mass or dermo-cosmetics

macro.risk: Raw material and input cost volatility
macro.description: Biobased/sustainable raw material sourcing, recycled packaging material costs and supply shortages are an identified risk as the Group pursues ecodesign and sustainability commitments

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global beauty market continues to be described by L'Oreal and peers as a 'resilient exception' amid macro and geopolitical disruption, with mid-single-digit underlying growth expected industry-wide for 2026, premiumisation and dermocosmetics/longevity trends as the strongest sub-segment drivers, and China/Asia Travel Retail recovery (still gradual, led by the premium/selective segment and e-commerce) as the key swing factor for the luxury end of the market.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-low; beauty/personal care is viewed as a defensive-leaning consumer staple relative to broader discretionary retail, but the prestige/Luxe division and Travel Retail channel carry meaningfully higher cyclicality tied to affluent-consumer and outbound-travel/tourism spending, as evidenced by North Asia Luxe's underperformance during 2023-2025's China slowdown
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (manageable balance-sheet leverage, strong free cash flow of ~EUR7.2bn net cash flow in 2025, up 7.8%), but elevated rates can indirectly dampen discretionary prestige-beauty demand and increase financing costs on gross debt (H1 2026 finance costs on gross debt rose to EUR259m from EUR181m a year earlier)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High; reports in EUR but generates the large majority of sales outside the eurozone (North America, North Asia, Latin America, SAPMENA-SSA together ~66% of FY2025 sales), making reported growth rates and margins sensitive to USD, RMB and emerging-market currency moves versus the euro; centrally managed via forward contracts/options but residual volatility remains material to reported (vs like-for-like) results
key_input_costs: Biobased, recycled and sustainably sourced raw materials and packaging (plastics, actives)
Advertising and media costs (~32% of sales, the Group's largest controllable cost line)
Energy and logistics for 37 factories and 160 distribution centres
Tariffs/customs duties on cross-border manufacturing and distribution
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: Increasingly complex and fragmented: EU REACH/CLP cosmetic safety rules, CSRD sustainability reporting (now fully integrated into L'Oreal's 2025 Universal Registration Document), evolving AI governance, tightening global data-protection regimes, and rising US product-liability litigation exposure are all flagged by the Group as rising-cost but currently well-managed risk categories.

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 sales reached EUR23.78bn, +6.8% like-for-like (+6.5% adjusted LFL) and +5.8% reported; operating margin hit a first-half record of 21.3% (up 20bp); diluted EPS excluding non-recurring items rose +4.8% to EUR7.40; all four divisions posted operating margins above 22%; gross margin expanded to 74.8%. Non-recurring items included EUR169m of product liability costs and a EUR188m exceptional French tax surcharge.

L'Oreal signed a 50-year exclusive worldwide licence with Kering for the creation, development and distribution of Gucci beauty/fragrance products, effective 1 July 2027 (subject to regulatory approval), following Kering's early buy-back of Coty's existing Gucci Beaute licence; extends L'Oreal's existing Kering beauty relationship (Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga, Creed, acquired via the Kering Beaute deal that closed 31 March 2026).

L'Oreal signed an agreement to acquire a majority stake in Innovist, a leading personal-care player in India, to strengthen its position in the fast-growing Indian beauty market; expected to complete within months of signing, subject to regulatory approval.

Annual General Meeting held; all proposed resolutions adopted, including continuation of a share buyback mandate (up to EUR500m or 2 million shares, cancelled upon repurchase) and governance committee changes (Pablo Isla and Catherine Olivry joining the Human Resources and Remuneration Committee).

L'Oreal completed the acquisition of Kering Beaute, including the House of Creed and 50-year exclusive licences for Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga beauty/fragrance products, as announced 19 October 2025; brands consolidated in the financial statements from the beginning of April 2026.

2025 Universal Registration Document filed with the AMF, reporting FY2025 sales of EUR44.05bn (+4.0% LFL, +1.3% reported), operating margin of 20.2% (up 20bp), EPS excluding non-recurring items of EUR12.71 (+0.4%), dividend per share of EUR7.20 (+2.9%), and net cash flow of EUR7.2bn (+7.8%); 2025 was described by CEO Nicolas Hieronimus as 'a record year for M&A' and 'a year of deep transformation, with record investments' in AI and tech.

Completed the increase of L'Oreal's stake in Galderma (medical/aesthetic dermatology company) from 10% to 20%, a transaction announced 8 December 2025; L'Oreal stated it does not intend to further increase this stake.

L'Oreal completed acquisitions of Dr.G (Korean dermocosmetics brand), Medik8 (UK medicalised skincare) and Color Wow (US premium hair-styling brand) during 2025, described as 'filling strategic gaps' in the portfolio ahead of the larger Kering Beaute deal.

items.target: Another year of growth in sales and profit, continuing to outperform the beauty market
items.notes: CEO Nicolas Hieronimus stated in the H1 2026 Prospects section: 'we are confident that demand for beauty remains strong... we believe that we are uniquely well equipped to continue outperforming the market and despite the current context achieving another year of growth in sales and profit.' No specific numerical full-year target is disclosed; L'Oreal does not issue formal quantitative annual guidance (consistent with historical practice), instead framing qualitative confidence in continued market outperformance.

items.target: Approximately -0.6% full-year impact on sales if June 2026 rates persist
items.notes: Based on extrapolating the 30 June 2026 EUR/USD rate of 1.1395 through year-end; H1 2026 currency impact was already -2.8% on reported sales growth.
H1 2026 commentary notes the Chinese selective/Travel Retail market 'continued to gradually improve,' with L'Oreal outperforming the market nearly three-fold in China during H1 2026.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Nicolas Hieronimus characterised H1 2026 as 'a strong first half' with growth 'broad-based across all categories, divisions, and regions,' driven by 'the seamless execution of our innovation strategy and our market-beating growth in e-commerce.' He highlighted gross margin expansion from volume growth and mix improvement, cost control enabling a 70bp increase in brand-building (A&P) investment, and a record first-half operating margin of 21.3%. He emphasized the strengthened brand portfolio (notably the addition of Kering Beaute), an innovation engine 'firing on all cylinders' aided by AI, and digital/offline channel execution as the basis for confidence in continued market outperformance into H2 2026, 'despite the current context.' In the FY2025 annual report, Hieronimus described 2025 as 'a year of deep transformation, with record investments in building our future growth engines,' citing record AI/tech investment, a record 725 patents filed, and 'a record year for M&A.'

bull_case: Unmatched global scale and portfolio diversification across four divisions, five regions and ~40 brands spanning every price tier give L'Oreal structurally lower single-segment risk than any pure-play peer, and it became the #1 beauty player across all five of its geographic regions in 2025

Consistent outperformance of the global beauty market (every division growing like-for-like in FY2025 and accelerating further in H1 2026 to +6.8% LFL) with margin expansion rather than margin trade-off -- operating margin reached a record 20.2% in FY2025 and a first-half record 21.3% in H1 2026

Record, well-targeted bolt-on M&A (Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Kering Beaute/Creed/Bottega Veneta/Balenciaga, a future 50-year Gucci licence, increased Galderma stake, Innovist in India) is systematically filling portfolio gaps in the fastest-growing beauty adjacencies (K-beauty, medicalised skincare, ultra-luxury fragrance, styling) while funded from strong internal cash flow (EUR7.2bn net cash flow in 2025, +7.8%)

Multiple embedded recovery catalysts not yet fully reflected in results: China/North Asia Travel Retail and the broader Chinese selective beauty market are gradually improving from a multi-year trough, and Professional Products/Dermatological Beauty are both compounding at double-digit like-for-like rates

Stable, long-term-oriented governance via the founding Bettencourt Meyers family's controlling influence (through Tethys) supports patient capital allocation and insulates the company from short-term activist pressure that affects some consumer-staples peers
bear_case: China/Asia Travel Retail recovery remains fragile and partial -- North Asia like-for-like growth was just +0.5% in FY2025 with L'Oreal Luxe flat on a reported basis, and any renewed Chinese consumer slowdown or disruption to outbound travel/duty-free spending would disproportionately hit the Group's highest-margin segment

Persistent currency headwinds convert strong underlying (like-for-like) growth into much weaker reported growth and EPS (e.g., North America -0.7% reported vs +3.4% LFL in FY2025; FY2025 EPS excluding non-recurring items grew only +0.4%; H1 2026 currency drag was -2.8% on sales), creating a gap between the operational growth story and what flows through to reported euro-denominated results

Unusually heavy and concentrated 2025-2026 M&A activity (Kering Beaute, Galderma stake increase, Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Innovist, the pending Gucci licence) raises integration, goodwill/intangible impairment and management-attention risk simultaneously across multiple deals, with net financial investment outflows of over EUR4.2bn in H1 2026 alone pressuring residual cash flow (-EUR9.8bn in H1 2026 versus +EUR0.3bn in H1 2025)

Intensifying competition from indie/DTC beauty brands (Rare Beauty, Fenty Beauty, e.l.f. Beauty) and fast-moving Chinese domestic champions (Proya, Bloomage) that can launch and iterate faster than a company of L'Oreal's scale, combined with growing dependence on Amazon and other large marketplaces that hold increasing retail leverage

Elevated US product-liability litigation exposure (EUR169m of related non-recurring costs in H1 2026 alone) and a complex, fragmented global regulatory environment (REACH/CLP, CSRD, AI governance, data protection) that continues to raise compliance costs across 75+ countries of operation
